subject: Escalation: clawback waiver request for Mina Haddad - conditional approval needed
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: clawback waiver for Mina Haddad (equity refresh)

Hi Logan —

Quick context: Mina Haddad (Engineering, Platform) received an equity refresh (approved May 2027) tied to midcycle performance. After payroll closed we discovered an HR admin flag that would technically trigger a 12-month clawback provision because the role change paperwork landed after the vesting effective date. This is a paperwork timing issue rather than performance or misconduct.

Why I'm asking for a waiver:
- Retention risk: Mina is a key contributor on the KV cache project; manager has escalated she is actively entertaining counteroffers.
- Performance: documented above-expectations rating and clear stretch scope; see attached performance_notes.docx.
- Root cause: admin lag between manager approval and People Ops upload; not an exceptional facts case.

Ask: executive approval to waive the 12-month clawback for Mina's May refresh, or alternatively approve a partial waiver (75% now, 25% deferred 6 months) to reduce risk while preserving policy guardrails.

I've attached the comp_adjustment_form.pdf and performance_notes.docx. Laura — can you confirm the exact policy language and any precedent? If we can get conditional sign-off (legal and finance approval), we'll draft the waiver memo.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Sr. People Business Partner
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- comp_adjustment_form.pdf (form filled by manager)
- performance_notes.docx (manager summary, examples)
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-19T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: clawback waiver for Mina Haddad (equity refresh)

Thanks Marissa — good write-up. A few quick questions before I escalate to legal/finance:

1) Is the manager willing to accept a deferred tranche if we want compromise? If so, what timeline feels reasonable to reduce churn risk?
2) Any prior waivers in EMEA/us in the last 12 months we can point to (precedent)?
3) Any material customer-facing compliance or audit exposure if we waive?

My preliminary view: approve a time-limited partial waiver (75% immediate / 25% deferred 6 months) subject to a signed recoupment-free clause removed only for admin-errors. That preserves policy for misconduct while addressing retention.

Vivek — looping you for budget/finance sign-off and to confirm if this approach is acceptable from a controls perspective. Laura — please flag any People Ops process changes that can prevent repeat. CC-ing Mina so she's aware of the request and next steps.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Head of People Operations (Interim)
Redwood Inference

- Signed waiver memo routed through Legal (legal@brightlaw.com) and Finance (Vivek).

Appreciate the context and Laura's precedent work. Finance is willing to approve a conditional waiver with the following constraints:

1) Immediate payout capped at 80% of the approved refresh amount; remaining 20% deferred for 6 months.
2) Manager attestation that the delay was administrative (signed and timestamped).
3) Legal must draft a waiver memo that explicitly excludes misconduct forgiveness — waiver applies strictly to timing/admin errors.
4) We will record the decision in the comp_exceptions ledger and include a clawback trigger if post-hire investigation yields cause.

If Legal can turn the memo around this afternoon, I will sign the finance section. Logan — please confirm manager buy-in on the 80/20 split so we can finalize.

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Finance & Operations
Redwood Inference

Note: Mina Haddad (cc'd) — we are working to minimize disruption. You should expect a short waiver memo for signature once Legal finalizes wording. If you have questions about timing or the deferred tranche, reply and we'll coordinate.
